The fixed configuration blocks send_email to non-allowlisted domains and DLP on secrets. So the exfiltration path is blocked → not_exploitable_as_configured likely true. But still give a vector for what remains: injection could still influence read_file within session (direct language I, session S). CVSS: AV:N (page fetched remotely), AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:P (user must ask to fetch page... passive), VC:L/VI:L? Impact: none remaining really — email blocked, DLP, fetch allowlist, sanitize_output redacts secrets. So residual impact minimal: VC:N VI:N VA:N, SC:N SI:N SA:N.

Score LC=I (indirect injection via fetched page), CP: session context — testing? Briefing doesn't confirm session testing; memory exists (remember tool) but path doesn't store. Context persists in session only → S. AP=C (relays across components same principal). RH: no evaluator/reward channel on path; no evidence of isolation test — reachable_proxy false? There's no evaluator at all... but classify_rh needs facts. reachable_proxy: false, isolation_verified: null → X? Set reachable_proxy null, isolation_verified null → X. ES: tools are all built-in allowlisted, but argument schemas... validate_args off in baseline but fixed config only sets s3 flags. Extension surface: fixed allowlist? All 12 built-ins offered; args unvalidated → M? ES=W per "not independently constrained"? Fixed config constrains email destinations. I'll say M (allowlisted but argument gaps). Actually baseline hardening empty but fixed s3 adds email_domains, dlp, sanitize_output, fetch allowlist. That's least-privilege-ish bindings enforced... but only for email/fetch. Other tools unvalidated. M.

RH facts: no evaluator in app → reachable_proxy false? No test confirming isolation. isolation_verified null → X. Set verified_episodes 0, episodes null.

CVSS vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N. UI:P passive — user must ask agent to fetch the page (normal use). Actually attacker must get user to fetch attacker-editable page; user does normal task → passive.

AIVSS: LC=I, CP=S, AP=C, RH=X, ES=M.

Applicability: model_directed_goal_pursuit: true (agent loops tools per goal), selects_or_sequences_actions: true. High confidence.

Automatable: attack needs model compliance with injection — No? Steps automated once triggered but depends on model obeying injected text and user fetching page. I'll say No.

Technical impact: Partial (secret file disclosure, not total system).
